head_provenance.not_inherited: No verdict was carried over from the previous issue of this file. All 16 K items were re-executed at this HEAD.

decision_rationale: GO_WITH_CONDITIONS. The two K items that previously FAILED (launch_scope, artifact_path_traversal) now PASS: CR-003 and RISK-1 wired the containment guard, re-measured here at 7/7. All 16 K items are PASS and 0 are NOT_MEASURED. The verdict is still not GO, for two reasons that are NOT security-blockers and NOT this gate's to sign: the two HOST dependencies (AEGIS-F5 absent NVIDIA driver, AEGIS-F6 no scheduled task) leave restart recovery and GPU performance unmeasured, and four evidence inputs the aggregator requires do not exist. A gate that reported GO here would be claiming a release readiness it cannot measure.
blockers_are_not_p0_p2: AEGIS-F1 is HIGH but is NOT a P0-P2 blocker: it needs a valid control token AND a signed v2 directive AND a resolvable node+WorkBuddy CLI. No unauthenticated or remote party can reach it, and no automatic side-effect actuator exists or is enabled.

k_section.evidence: 1601 files scanned for 8 credential families. 144 pattern hits reduce to 12 unique strings, all synthetic redaction fixtures originating at packages/jcc_core/tests/test_redaction_values.py:78-85; the rest are copies in artifacts/acceptance snapshots. Zero .env values appear in any scanned file. redact() masks api_key/password; the server never interpolates a token into a log record.

27 mutating routes; every one returns 401/403 with no token. Authorization: Bearer OVERRIDES X-JCC-Token, and a wrong bearer paired with a VALID X-JCC-Token returns 403, so there is no header-smuggling path. Empty bearer 403; trailing space 403 (no trimming). Undeclared open GET routes = 0 (28 declared / 27 served). /docs and /openapi.json 404.

check_bind_host refuses 0.0.0.0, ::, 192.168.1.5, example.com and '0' with SystemExit, accepting only 127.0.0.1/127.0.0.2/localhost/::1. run.py hardcodes BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1 and passes it to uvicorn.run, so config cannot move the listener. Both config files declare host 127.0.0.1 and an explicit CORS allowlist with no '*'. No external listener was observed.

Baseline sign+verify returns (True,'ok'). A tampered-params directive returns BAD_SIGNATURE. v2 signature offered to a v1 verifier returns BAD_SIGNATURE (no downgrade). An unknown form raises ValueError against the closed set {v1,v2} and is never defaulted. A blank/unset key makes load_signing_key return None, and the signer reports available=False rather than emitting a fake signature.

Directive kernel: the same nonce verifies once then returns REPLAY. Webhook receiver: a repeated delivery_id is rejected with reason='replay', and the replay check runs AFTER signature so unauthenticated traffic cannot poison the cache. A body-swap and an agent-header-swap are both rejected as bad_signature.
issued_at far in the past -> EXPIRED. issued_at in the future beyond the 30s skew allowance -> NOT_YET_VALID. The receiver's separate window rejects a stale timestamp with timestamp_out_of_window.

directive_gate runs 9 ordered checks; check 5 (session) binds the directive's session to the intent's mission, so a directive naming a different project/mission returns SESSION_MISMATCH before any effect.

check 6 (capability) requires exactly CAPABILITY_USER_LAUNCH and returns CAPABILITY_DENIED for anything else. The launch template registry is bound by template_registry_digest into the signed params, so an adapter outside the registry cannot be substituted without breaking the signature.

An event with agent='not_a_real_agent' returns 422, not 2xx. An envelope with no session_id returns 422, so cwd cannot become the identity (JCC contract rule 7). A garbage envelope returns 422. The renderer classifier returns UNKNOWN for an empty string and for an unrecognised renderer -- it never folds 'not identified' into HARDWARE.

host_launcher.py contains zero shell=True call sites; the single subprocess.Popen site passes an argv list. A goal of '; rm -rf / # $(whoami) `id` && calc.exe' became ONE argv element out of 14, so the metacharacters are data and are never interpreted by a shell.

Template param_flags build ['--flag', value] as separate list elements; no f-string shell line is constructed anywhere in the launcher. The joined argv is only ever used for an args_hash and for logging, never re-split into a shell.

/api/health reports actuation_enabled=False, localhost_only=True, policy_version=p3.0.0. Both config files carry actuation.enabled=false with allowed_actions=[]. Jev scores, Policy emits directives, the Actuator refuses every side-effect.

product_findings.summary: A non-ASCII control token raises an unhandled TypeError in require_control_token (hmac.compare_digest rejects non-ASCII str).
product_findings.repro: Raw ASGI POST /api/pause with header x-jcc-token: \xe4\xb8\xad\xe6\x96\x87 raises TypeError. httpx masks this with its own UnicodeEncodeError, so it must be driven at the ASGI layer.
product_findings.confidentiality_impact: NONE. The request is still refused; no token is accepted that should not be. This is an availability/robustness defect: an unhandled exception instead of a 403.
product_findings.recommended_fix: Coerce both operands to bytes, or wrap the compare in try/except TypeError and fall through to 403.
product_findings.recommendation: FIX IT -- it is a 3-line change in server.py and the failure mode is an unhandled exception in the auth path.

product_findings.summary: .env declares JCC_CONTROL_TOKEN, JCC_CONFIG and JEV_API_KEY with EMPTY values, and the host exports no JCC_*/JEV_* variables at all.
product_findings.why: This is fail-CLOSED and therefore correct: an unset or empty token yields '' which require_control_token rejects, so the control plane is LOCKED rather than open. All 27 mutating routes were confirmed to refuse.
product_findings.residual_risk: Operational only: an operator may believe a token is configured when the file says otherwise, and an empty JEV_API_KEY means the real provider cannot authenticate.
product_findings.recommended_fix: Expose control_token_configured (a boolean) on /api/health so the fact is visible without leaking any value.
product_findings.recommendation: WORTH FIXING but not urgent and not a security defect. The health flag is a 2-line change and turns a silent misconfiguration into a visible one. Do NOT let it read the token value.

product_findings.summary: SessionIsolation._map in the webhook receiver has no TTL, no maxsize and no eviction, unlike ReplayCache.
product_findings.impact: Unbounded growth on a long-lived receiver; an attacker holding the shared webhook secret could deliberately grow the cross-agent binding table. Post-authentication only.
product_findings.recommended_fix: Give it the same ttl+maxsize treatment as ReplayCache, or derive bindings from the audit table.
product_findings.recommendation: FIX WHEN CONVENIENT -- low urgency, small change, and it removes an unbounded map from a security component.

verification_discipline.note: Two of my own probes were wrong before they were right. Both are recorded because a gate that hides its own broken tests cannot be audited.
self_corrections: The write-side check first reported FAIL because my own filter treated the scope base D:\jev as an out-of-scope probe. The product was correct; the assertion was wrong.

The launch-side and existence-oracle sections first reported PASS VACUOUSLY: I called validate_project_root(raw) without its keyword-only `roots` argument, every call raised TypeError, and my handler counted TypeError as REFUSED. A test that passes because the call was malformed proves nothing. Now the real roots are passed and a TypeError is treated as FAILURE.
verification_discipline.vacuous_pass_lesson: A refusal-shaped exception from a malformed call is indistinguishable from a real refusal unless the expected exception type is asserted explicitly. This is the same class as the CRLF false positive: the check appeared to pass for a reason unrelated to the property under test. A third instance of the same shape was caught in this very correction: a shell-escaped comparison string made every CR look like a lone CR. Method errors keep arriving in the same family: a check that passes or fails for a reason unrelated to the property under test.

normalisation_correction.what_was_wrong: Aegis verified these artefacts with tr -d '\r' and reported MATCH. That rule deletes EVERY CR, not only the CRLF one, so an in-band CR injection normalises to the same bytes as a clean file -- a FALSE NEGATIVE, not a labelling nicety.
normalisation_correction.independently_reproduced: HEAD 'ab\r\n' -> 61 62 0a; WORK 'a\rb\r\n' -> tr: 61 62 0a (MATCH, damage hidden) vs sed 's/\r$//': 61 0d 62 0a (DIFFER, caught). Verified on this host.
normalisation_correction.do_any_verdicts_change: No. Both rules agree on all three artefacts, because the tree contains zero lone CRs. The earlier MATCH results were right BY LUCK, not by correctness: on a tree with no lone CR the unsound rule and the sound rule coincide. A correct conclusion reached by an unsound method is not a verified result.
